entries.source: PANGERL, Goldenkron (=FRA II/37, Wien 1872) S. 481-483, 1454 VIII 21
entries.german:
Vidimus bezeichneter Urkunden des Königs und Kaisers Sigmund, auf die Verpfändung der Herrschaften Prachatitz und Wallern bezüglich, darunter namentlich auch die Urkunde ddto. Prag, 1. Juni, 1431. (N. CLXXXV.)

Nos Paulus miseratione divina ordinis Cisterciensis monasterii beatae virginis Altivadensis, Gerhardus eiusdem ordinis monasterii Sanctae Coronae abbates, Wilhelmus iunior de Risenbergk et de Rabie, Wilhelmus de Hersstain barones inclyti regni Bohemiae, Przibl de Mladiegowicz et Erasmus de Michnicz 1 protunc purgravius castri Maydstain praesentis scripti patrocinio publice recognoscimus et profitemur, quod cum magnifici et excellentes domini dominus Vlricus de Rosenberk, Henricus, Johannes et Jodocus 2 fratres germani et filii domini Vlrici praescripti de Rosenberk unanimi omnium consensu, beneplacito et voluntate specialibus votivis nos accersiri censuerunt precibus, quatenus omnes et singuli et singulariter omnes sua personali praesentia ad castrum habitationis ipsorum Crumpnaw adeundi dare velimus operam efficacem. Nobis itaque in eodem Castro Crumpnaw constitutis plurimas divi Sigismundi Romanorum imperatoris invictissimi ac Hungariae et Bohemiae regis etc. litteras suae magestatis sigillo pendenti munitas obtulerunt in et super plurium bonorum obligationibus et certis debitis atque dampnis priscis temporibus intuitu suae magestatis perceptis, quas quidem pro pulcro stilo et modulo ac proportione confectas litteras sanas et integras, non rasas aut cancellatas, nec in aliqua sui , parte suspectas, sed omni prorsus vitio et defectu ac suspicione carentes solertissime coperimus (sic, comperimus) esse directas, quarum quidem litterarum tenor de verbo ad verbum per omnia sequitur et est talis: (Folgt nun der Wortlaut [theils in lateinischer theils in böhmischer Sprache] der auf die Verpfändung der Herrschaften Prachatitz und Wallern [sonst dem Wyschehrader Capitel gehörig] so wie gewisser Stift-Goldenkroner Dörfer bezüglichen Urkunden des Königs Sigmund ddto. Kuttenberg, 21. December [Thomas], 1421 - Prag, 5. Mai [Sonntag nach Kreuzerfindung], 1437 - Prag, 1. Juni, 1437 - abermals eine ddto. Prag, 1. Juni [Samst. nach Dreifalt.] 1437, welche Urkunde allein in diesem Urkundenbuche abgedruckt erscheint - Passau, 17. Octob. [Samst. nach Galli], 1422 - Kuttenberg, 31. Dec. [Silvester], 1421.) Nos itaque Paulus et Gerhardus abbates, Wilhelmus iunior de Rysenberk et de Rabie et Wilhelmus de Hersstain barones, Przibl et Erasmus omnes et singuli suprascripti praeexpressis et clarius de verbo ad verbum singulis descriptis litteris sic ut praemittitur in forma visis, perlectis, auditis et diligenter auscultatis, ad vota dictorum dominorum de Rosenbergk et beneplacitum speciale hanc litteram vidimus, non per errorem aut inprovide sed animo deliberato et de certa omnium nostrum scientia conficere decrevimus et conficimus per praesentes. In cuius rei evidens testimonium perpetuo firmius valiturum sigilla nostra propria cum pleno scitu et voluntate duximus appendenda. Datum in Castro Crumpnaw anno a nativitate domini millesimo quadringentesimo quinquagesimo quarto, feria quarta ante sancti Bartholomey apostoli.
entries.english:
Vidimus of specified charters of Sigmund, Römischer Kaiser und König von Ungarn und Böhmen concerning the pledging of the lordships of Prachatitz and Wallern, including especially the charter dated Prague, 1 June 1431 (no. CLXXXV).

We, Paulus, by divine mercy abbot of the Cistercian monastery of the Blessed Virgin at Altovad, and Gerhard, abbot of the monastery of the same order at Santa Corona; Wilhelm der Jüngere von Risenberg and Rabie and Wilhelm von Hersstain, barons of the illustrious Kingdom of Bohemia; Przibl von Mladiegowicz; and Erasmus von Michnicz, then burgrave of Maydstain Castle, publicly acknowledge and declare by this instrument that the illustrious and distinguished lords Ulrich von Rosenberg, Heinrich, Johannes, and Jodocus, full brothers and sons of the aforesaid Herr Ulrich von Rosenberg, unanimously and of their own accord summoned us by special and earnest petition, asking each and every one of us to come in person to their residence, Crumpnaw Castle.

When we had assembled at that castle, they presented to us numerous letters of His Majesty, the late Sigismund, most invincible Roman Emperor and König von Ungarn und Böhmen, bearing his pendant seal, concerning the pledging of various properties, certain debts, and losses incurred in earlier times in consideration of His Majesty. We carefully found those letters, which were executed in fine form and due proportion, to be sound and complete, neither erased nor cancelled, suspect in no part, and entirely free of defect, fault, or suspicion. The tenor of those letters follows here word for word in every respect.

[The source then notes that the texts, partly in Latin and partly in Czech, concern the pledging of the lordships of Prachatitz and Wallern, otherwise belonging to the Vyšehrad chapter, and certain villages of Goldenkron Abbey. The listed dates are Kuttenberg, 21 December 1421; Prague, 5 May 1437; Prague, 1 June 1437; another charter dated Prague, 1 June 1437 (the only one printed in this charter book); Passau, 17 October 1422; and Kuttenberg, 31 December 1421.]

Therefore, we, the abbots Paulus and Gerhard, Wilhelm der Jüngere von Risenberg and Rabie, Wilhelm von Hersstain, Przibl, and Erasmus, having seen, read, heard, and diligently listened to the aforesaid letters, as described above and individually transcribed more fully word for word, have decided, in accordance with the wishes and particular request of the said lords von Rosenberg, to prepare this instrument—not by mistake or carelessness, but deliberately and with the certain knowledge of us all—and by this document we do so. As clear and lasting evidence of this matter, we have caused our own seals to be appended with the full knowledge and consent of us all. Given at Crumpnaw Castle in the year of the Herr 1454, on the Wednesday before the feast of Saint Bartholomew the Apostle.

Two small seals in red wax hang from parchment strips. (a) A shield bearing a rose; the legend reads “Sigillum Domini Ulrici de Rozmberg.” (b) A similar seal; the legend reads “S. Jan z Rosenbergka.”
